column2: Late because it is on hold
EAMOne: scan for overdue work orders
The actual start less the planned start. Negative means it started early.
Scan complete: %(t)d orders overdue, %(d)d new notifications sent.
The actual hours worked less the planned span. Positive means it took longer than expected.
Order "%(ten)s" at %(vt)s is %(g).0f hours overdue (planned finish %(h)s).

Updated by cron. NOT a computed field: "is it overdue yet" depends on what time it is now, and the present moment cannot sit inside @api.depends — declared as a stored computed field, the flag would stand still for ever with nothing to say so.

A red row is late through being forgotten — the person responsible has been sent the job. A yellow row is late because it is waiting on someone outside: that is a supply chain problem rather than the fitter's, so the system does not chase them.

Overdue, but the order is on hold. That is a supply chain problem rather than the fitter's, so NO notification is sent — reminding someone every day about something they cannot solve is the fastest way to make them ignore every notification afterwards.

Four dates side by side — planned and actual, start and finish — plus three variances computed in advance. Switch to calendar for a week or month view, kanban to drag states, and pivot to see who is overloaded.
